resources.string: Alerts when an opt-out request is detected in an incoming message.
Temporary notices shown while a message is being checked in the background.

SMS Filter watches incoming text messages for opt-out requests from senders who are not in your contacts, and replies automatically so you stop hearing from them.\n\nMessages from people you know are always ignored. Your contacts are never copied or uploaded — every check happens on this phone, in real time.
SMS Filter needs these permissions to work. You cannot continue until the required ones are granted.
Lets the app see incoming messages so it can detect opt-out requests. Without this the app cannot function.
Lets the app send the one-word \"stop\" or \"end\" reply on your behalf.
Lets the app tell you when it has detected an opt-out request.
Lets the app recognise people you know so it never replies to them. If you skip this, every sender is treated as unknown.
Android will no longer show the permission prompt for this. Grant it in App Settings, then return here — the app will detect it automatically.
Contacts access is denied, so every sender will be treated as unknown. You can grant it later in Settings.
Checking that the app can read your contacts to recognise people you know.
Google Contacts: Not accessible — permission denied. You can grant it later from Settings.

Auto-reply is ON by default — SMS Filter will automatically send a one-word \"stop\" or \"end\" reply when it detects an opt-out message from an unknown sender. You can switch to detection-only mode anytime in Settings.
HubSpot CRM is optional and is not set up here. You will be offered it once after setup, and can always connect it later from Settings.
Settings are implemented in the next phase.
The detection log is implemented in the next phase.
